cases.goal: Make /continue safely continue the user's current work without surprising task switches.

evidence_catalog.text: The interactive app owns /continue command routing and current task focus.
Session history can list and restore previously saved tasks.
Terminal theme rendering controls colors and borders only.
History is convenience state and cannot invent mutation authority.
Changing mutation focus to historical work requires an explicit resume selection and re-attestation.
The most recently written history entry always owns current mutation focus.
Implicit history fallback can resume and mutate a different task than the user intended.
Incorrect focus restoration can contribute to duplicate execution or duplicate publication attempts.
A palette color mismatch can make /continue harder to read.
The user-visible meaning of continue versus explicit history resume must be resolved rather than inferred from recency.
Assume the newest safely resumable history item is equivalent to the user's current task.
Assume any behavior is acceptable if the existing command tests pass.

cases.goal: Document and surface the platforms on which normal deterministic WCO task execution is actually supported.

evidence_catalog.text: Setup reports user-facing readiness and recovery guidance.
Deterministic verification uses Bubblewrap and rejects non-Linux hosts.
README contains install and run examples for multiple shells.
Reviewer mode freezes Sol/Terra selection per run.
A package being installable on a host does not imply normal task verification is executable on that host.
Normal deterministic verification must fail closed when required isolation is unavailable.
Native Windows/macOS users can infer full support from successful installation and fail only after starting work.
Reviewer selection might reveal a provider credential.
The product claim must distinguish native host support from WSL/Linux execution support.
Assume a PowerShell install example means normal native Windows task execution is supported.
Assume Bubblewrap can be skipped when verification commands are simple.

cases.goal: Ensure first interactive use cannot leave an orphan task when ChatGPT authorization is cancelled or unavailable.

evidence_catalog.text: The authorization boundary can perform official interactive sign-in only on eligible TTY use.
Authoring job creation persists durable task state.
CLI help prints commands but does not own authorization state.
Interactive authorization must complete before durable task creation on first use.
CI and non-interactive callers must never open browser authorization.
Creating task state before cancelled authorization can strand an AUTHORING session and trap the next goal.
Long help output can slow shell startup.
The flow must distinguish eligible interactive use from non-interactive/provider-boundary failure.
Assume it is harmless to create the durable job first and authorize immediately afterward.
Assume CI may open a browser if credentials are missing.

cases.goal: Allow global reviewer preference changes without silently changing the reviewer of an already prepared AUTOPILOT run after restart.

evidence_catalog.text: The UI-level reviewer preference can be changed for future tasks.
Prepared runs persist a reviewer selection inside the canonical run directory.
Deterministic verification is provider-independent.
A prepared run's reviewer selection is frozen exactly once and resume must use that immutable selection.
Mutable global reviewer preference applies to new runs, not existing prepared runs.
Reading global mode on resume can change provider/model authority after work was prepared.
Unit tests can run in a different filename order.
Resume must distinguish a prepared run with frozen reviewer authority from a not-yet-prepared task.
Assume current global /mode is the desired reviewer whenever a run resumes.
Assume Sol/high should replace a stored reviewer because it is the default.

cases.goal: Recover safely after a crash around Draft PR publication without duplicating or silently retargeting the published result.

evidence_catalog.text: Publisher binds local publication to exact remote/base/head identities.
Draft PR receipts persist the exact PR number, branch and published commit identity.
TUI theme state is reloaded after restart.
Recovery must re-attest the exact expected branch and head, not accept any PR that happens to contain equivalent code.
Exact durable pushed state may be adopted idempotently; ambiguous publication must not be blindly replayed.
Blind retry after a crash can create a second Draft PR or duplicate push.
Accepting a different PR/branch with the same commit can silently retarget publication authority.
Recovery must determine whether the remote side effect happened before the durable local checkpoint completed.
Assume repeating publish/create-PR is always safe because Git operations are idempotent.
Assume matching only the commit SHA is enough to adopt any existing PR.

cases.goal: Allow status/pause interaction while a task runs without introducing a second mutation owner or unsafe immediate interruption.

evidence_catalog.text: Interactive task slot enforces one background mutation owner.
Pause is cooperative and takes effect at a safe lifecycle boundary.
Command history supports Up-arrow and search behavior.
At most one interactive worker may own mutation at a time.
Pause must preserve durable progress and may not pretend the task is paused before a safe boundary is reached.
Launching resume/run while the current worker still owns mutation can create concurrent side effects.
Reporting paused before ownership is safely released can make exit/restart unsafe.
The UI must distinguish a requested pause from a durably reached paused state.
Assume aborting the active operation immediately is equivalent to a safe durable pause.
Assume /status needs a second worker because the current worker is busy.
